subject: Styx 5xx debrief & commitments (service-level RCA)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: accountops@stellarretail.com
Cc: rachel.kim@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Styx model - elevated 5xx errors (early notice)

Hi Priya,

We detected a spike of 5xx / timeout errors originating from requests routed to the Styx-v2 model in the us-west region starting ~08:50 PST. Impact appears to affect approximately 0.9% of requests for the last 20 minutes (we're still refining counts).

What we've done so far: 
- Isolated the affected model variant (Styx-v2-quant32) and throttled new routing to that variant.
- Collected sample request IDs and logs attached (styx-5xx-sample-requests.txt).
- Engaged runtime & kernel teams for triage.

We don't have a full RCA yet — investigating whether this is an infrastructure-level issue (kernel fallback path) or a model-runtime interaction with the quantized execution path.

Immediate ask: can you confirm observable customer impact on your side (errors/failed requests, degraded UX)? Any sample request IDs you can share are helpful if they differ from what we captured.

I'll update every 30 minutes until we have mitigation/rollback. Apologies for the disruption — will prioritize restoring routes.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: styx-5xx-sample-requests.txt (text)
From: Priya Menon <accountops@stellarretail.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: rachel.kim@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:45:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Styx model - elevated 5xx errors (early notice)

Marcus — thanks for the heads up. We're seeing increased error rates and two customer-facing features are returning failures; attached are three request IDs from our logs that matched your timeframe: 9a7c, b1d2, f3e4.

Immediate ask: do you have an ETA for a mitigation or recommended temporary workaround? Our SREs are standing by. If you need us to flip routing on our side (to a different model id), we can coordinate.

Priya
Priya Menon
Head of Platform Ops, Stellar Retail
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:20:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Styx model - elevated 5xx errors (initial triage)

Marcus / team — quick triage notes (internal):
- Observed stack traces point to a kernel selector regression when handling quantized KV cache fills at certain sequence lengths; the quantized execution path can enter a slow path that times out under high concurrency.
- Affects Styx-v2-quant32 only; Styx-v2-fp16 unaffected.

Immediate mitigations we are running now (actioned at 10:15 PST):
1) Reroute customer traffic away from Styx-v2-quant32 to Styx-v2-fp16 (compatible for most workloads) — this is live for Stellar Retail.
2) Enabled a prefix-KV caching bypass for Styx-v2-quant32 to reduce cache fills while we patch the kernel selector.
3) Backstop: increase retry budget and extend graceful fallback to a smaller Styx-lite variant in the rare case of degraded outputs.

I've uploaded the short mitigation runbook to the thread (mitigation-runbook.pdf) with steps we used. Marcus — can you confirm the routing change succeeded for Stellar and whether error rates dropped?

Rachel
Rachel Kim
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Menon <accountops@stellarretail.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:05:22 -0800
Subject: Styx 5xx - interim findings and rollback status

Priya — following up with a more concrete status update and next steps.

What we found (interim):
- Root cause: an unintended change in the kernel-selection heuristic shipped in the runtime patch (2026.11.15) caused quantized KK cache fill logic to choose a fallback kernel that performs poorly under high-concurrency prefix lengths. When the chosen kernel hit a pathological branch, it produced blocking behavior leading to request timeouts (5xx).
- Scope: Affected only the Styx-v2-quant32 variant in us-west; other models and regions unaffected.

Fixes & timeline: 
- 11/18 10:15 PST: Rerouted Stellar to Styx-v2-fp16. Error rate for Stellar dropped from ~0.9% -> 0.02% within 25 minutes.
- 11/18 11:40 PST: Rolled back kernel-selector patch in us-west for quantized variants; monitoring confirmed stable behavior.
- 11/19 01:10 PST: Completed full rollback for all quantized variants in us-west and re-enabled normal routing after validation.

Attachments & artifacts: postmortem draft (postmortem-draft.md) uploaded; sample traces available in the Drive link.

Customer commitments:
- We will share the full postmortem and mitigation plan by 11/20 EOD.
- We will provide an SLA credit estimate after final impact analysis (we'll follow up on the exact amount).
- We opened INF-2217 to track improved kernel-selector unit tests and can share the JIRA with your engineering team on request.

Again — apologies for the disruption. If you want us to run a short smoke test on your staging workload (route ~1% of traffic back to Styx-v2-quant32 under watch), we can coordinate a narrow test window.

Ben Carter
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-draft.md
Links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcD_Postmortem_Styx
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Priya Menon <accountops@stellarretail.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Styx 5xx - final RCA & follow-ups

Priya — final update and commitments now that we've completed the internal postmortem and remediation.

Summary:
- Confirmed root cause: regression in kernel-selection heuristic (runtime 2026.11.15) that caused pathological kernel choices for quantized KV cache scenarios.
- Impact: ~0.9% elevated 5xx on affected variant for a ~3 hour window; Stellar Retail saw transient customer-facing failures which were mitigated by rerouting.

Actions taken (completed):
- Full rollback of the runtime change that introduced the regression (11/18–11/19).
- Added unit & integration tests around kernel selection and KV cache concurrency (tracked INF-2217).
- Improved monitoring alerting to trigger earlier prefix-KV anomaly detection thresholds.

Customer commitments (what we'll deliver):
- Final postmortem document (public-ready) posted to the link above by 11/20 EOD.
- SLA credit proposal within 3 business days after final impact analysis.
- Quarterly review with your SREs to discuss traffic shaping and fallback strategies (optional).

If you'd like a 30-minute walk-through next week of the postmortem and the technical changes, we're happy to schedule. Thank you for your patience — we're treating this as a high-priority reliability improvement across the runtime.

Regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
VP, Product Operations & Reliability
Redwood Inference
